name: Yangkaal
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only texts and comparative work (Evans 1995 Yangkaal text; Evans 2005 Kayardild and the Tangkic Languages); no grammar or phonology of Yangkaal itself

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 1985. Kayardild: the language of the Bentinck Islanders of north west Queensland. PhD thesis, Australian National University (open, ANU repository).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL7101.G39 K8 1992
sources.note: p.3: 'it seems best to classify Kayardild and Yangkaal as dialects of one language'. p.508 (App. C.3.2, Kayardild): 'Stress in Kayardild is non-contrastive.. Main stress falls on the first syllable'; secondary on non-initial long vowels / trill-closed syllables, penults, first syllable of compound members and of polysyllabic inflectional or any derivational suffix. p.551 (Text 7, the only Yangkaal text): 'The Yangkaal phonemic system is almost identical to Kayardild, the only important difference is the retention of pT */rl/.. The main difference lies in voice quality. Yangkaal, like Lardil,…

sources.note: Nothing; ethno-historical. Relevant for identity: 'the fissioning of the Yangkaal-Kayardild language into two distinct geographical dialects, as the Kaiadilt people moved to Bentinck Island'.

sources.citation: Round, Erich R. 2009. Kayardild Morphology, Phonology and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, Yale University (Zenodo 829761).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Full analysis of Kayardild stress (ch.5: trochaic feet, head foot leftmost, root-initial stress). Yangkaal appears only as 'Kayardild's closest relative' with data from Hale's 1960 fieldnotes (AIATSIS MS3172 items 6, 9, 10); no statement about Yangkaal stress.
